name: spend-guard
description: Detects balance-drain attacks on metered third-party services — SMS pumping, toll fraud, and runaway API spend.
long_description:
Attackers can turn any public form that triggers a paid third-party call into a payment terminal. SMS pumping (IRSF) is the common case: an attacker enumerates phone numbers in ranges they control, triggers verification messages, and collects the carrier revenue share. Nothing in a conventional security stack sees it — no port scan, no failed login, no CVE — because the attacker uses the form exactly as designed and the loss lands at a provider your server never talks to.

spend-guard polls provider billing APIs, learns a baseline, and scores independent detectors: unit cost, daily volume, previously unseen destinations, and balance burn rate. Containment requires two signals to agree, because the hard problem is not spotting expensive traffic — it is telling expensive-and-fraudulent from expensive-and-legitimate. Real users dialling international numbers look expensive too; what distinguishes fraud is shape, arriving as a volume spike into destinations with no history rather than spread across weeks.

The burn-rate detector escalates to critical when auto-recharge is enabled, since that removes the only natural ceiling on the attack.

Detection logic is pure and I/O-free, and the test suite replays a real incident: it must fire on the fraud waves and stay quiet on a genuinely expensive month of legitimate international signups.
keywords: sms pumping, IRSF, toll fraud, balance drain, auto-recharge, billing anomaly, twilio, spend monitoring
